name: the forest
title: A Quiet Forest
description: Tall trunks, close together. The sea is only a sound now.
Trunks stand close and the light thins. Behind you, the sea is only a sound.
Among tall trees the air goes still. You can barely hear the sea.

text: The trees close in again. The sea fades to a murmur.
The forest takes you in again.
Under the trees, the sea goes quiet.
Back under the trees. It is darker here, and still.
The forest again, dim and still.
Back in the green half-dark.
Under the trees the dark is total. You feel your way between the trunks.
In the forest at night you can't see your hands.
Pitch dark under the trees. You go slowly, hands out.
Dry branches everywhere.
Deadwood all around.
Plenty of dry branches still.
Somewhere ahead, water runs over stones.
From somewhere ahead comes the sound of running water.
You hear water trickling, somewhere deeper in.
The spring trickles between mossy stones.
The spring is still running over the stones.
You hear the spring before you see it.

explore.name: look around
explore._explore: look around: a pop-up with what you see (view lines whose 'when' holds) and the landmarks not explored yet; no time passes until you pick one

text: Tall trunks, close together. The light is dim and green.
Trees all around, close and still.
Trunks, moss, and a quiet that swallows the sea.
Dead branches lie among the roots, dry enough to burn.
Deadwood everywhere under the trees.
Fallen branches, dry and light, all around.

view.text: Somewhere ahead, water runs over stones.
The spring trickles between mossy stones.
Small trails run under the ferns.
Deeper in, something large lies across the forest floor.

nothingLeft: The trees all look the same now.
Nothing here you have not seen.

landmarks.label: the sound of water
text: Between mossy stones, a small spring. The water is clear and cold.
Water wells up between mossy stones: a spring, clear and cold.
You find where the sound comes from: a small spring among the stones. The water is clean.

landmarks.label: the small trails
text: Narrow trails wind through the undergrowth, too small for anything but rabbits. Droppings, fresh. A snare could take one.
In the morning light you see them: little paths through the ferns, worn by rabbits. Snares would catch them.
Low runs under the bracken, droppings along them. Rabbits. With cord you could set snares.

landmarks.label: the fallen oak
text: Deeper in, a fallen oak, soft with age. Pale mushrooms grow along its bark. Cut into logs and kept wet, it could grow more.
Collecting wood you came across it: a fallen oak, furred with moss, mushrooms all along it. Logs of it would grow them too.
An old oak lies where it fell, mushrooms in rows along the bark. Its wood could be made to grow more.

activities.name: collect wood
log: Dry branches snap underfoot.
Twigs crack under your feet.
You snap dead branches off a fallen tree.
An armful of deadwood.
You gather an armful of dry wood.
Deadwood, as much as you can carry.
Bark and twigs, dry enough to burn.
Dry bark peels off in strips.
Twigs and branches, light and dry.
activities._note: no exploring needed: the forest floor is full of deadwood

activities.name: chop wood
log: The axe bites. Chips fly. A young tree comes down.
You fell a thin trunk and cut it into lengths.
Stroke after stroke, until the trunk cracks and falls.

activities.name: strip bark
log: You score a young tree and peel the inner bark away in long, pale strips.
The bark comes away in strips, wet and stringy, as long as your arm.
You cut and peel, cut and peel, until you have a bundle of bark strips.

activities.name: drink water
log: Cold water from the spring, tasting of stone.
You cup your hands and drink. Cold, clean.
The water tastes of stone and moss.
You drink until your teeth ache.
You drink long and slow.
Cold water, as much as you want.
